DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 81 s. 2022 JUL 25 2022 MR. PABLO M. CRESPO SR. Secretary to the Mayor Municipality of Patnongon Province of Antique Dear Sec. Crespo Sr. This has reference to your letter dated 03 March 2022 wherein you are seeking this Department's legal opinion as to who has the review power over the executive order issued by the provincial governor. At the outset, we would like to invite your attention to Section 465(b)(I)(xii) of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", as amended (LGC), to wit: "SECTION 465. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions, and Compensation. — xxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the province and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the provincial governor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the provincial government, and in this connection, shall: xxx (xii) Furnish copies of executive orders issued bv him to the Office of the President within seventy-two (72) hours after their issuance:" Correspondingly, under Presidential Memorandum Circular No. 146 dated 19 February 1992, and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 92-17, it states that all Provincial Governors are hereby directed to course through the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government all the issuances and reports which the aforecited provisions of the LGC require them to submit to the Office of the President. In view thereof, the executive orders issued by provincial governors are reviewed by the Office of the President, having the mandate to supervise local government units (LGUs), despite their autonomous status, coursed through this Department pursuant "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

to Presidential Memorandum Circular No. 146, to examine, and provide comments and recommendation on whether the executive orders are compliant or consistent with existing laws. Note, however, that while this Department exercises general supervision over LGUs, we have no authority to declare invalid any ordinance, executive order issued by the local chief executives, or resolution of the local sanggunians, or any act committed by the members thereof which is alleged to be in violation of the LGC or other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action for Declaratory Relief before the proper court, in accordance with Section I, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court. Notwithstanding, we would like to stress that this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Undersec ry for Local Government OUSLG/ML1/LLLS-LRALLD/rjki.ep copy furnished: DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGE-NIERO Regional Director, DILG Region VI P. Aquino St., Fort San Pedro, Iloilo Page 2 of 2
